payload.scope: People made acceleration features to capture the curvature, the rate of change of the velocity, of a spectral feature sequence, adding the second-order dynamics of phoneme transitions to the feature vector.

definition.body: Acceleration features (delta-delta features) are the second temporal derivative of a sequence of base acoustic features, obtained by applying the same weighted least-squares line fit to the delta sequence. For a base feature f(t) and its delta d(t), the acceleration at frame t is the delta of d computed over the same sliding window of half-width K with the same weight vector: d2(t) = argmin_d sum_{k=-K}^{K} w(k) * (d(t+k) - (a*t + b))^2. Equivalently it is the second derivative (2a) of a quadratic least-squares fit to f over the window; for K=1 the weights [1,-2,1] annihilate constants and linear trends and respond only to curvature. Parameters: (1) the base feature sequence f(t) (typically MFCC); (2) the window half-width K (commonly K=2); (3) the weight vector (normalized [-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3] over the delta sequence for K=3). Persistence: the third block of the standard 39-dimensional HMM feature vector (12 static + 12 delta + 12 acceleration) in Kaldi compute-vad-and-extract-features and HTK HCopy, and as the delta operator applied twice in librosa. e.g.: the delta-delta block of the 39-dimensional feature vector in Kaldi compute-vad-and-extract-features for triphone HMMs; the acceleration dimensions computed by applying librosa.feature.delta twice to an MFCC sequence; the 12 delta-delta dimensions of HTK HCopy's standard MFCC+delta+delta-delta feature string | not: delta-features (first-order velocity, not curvature); static MFCC (no temporal derivative); delta-cepstral-coefficients (raw cepstral first differences, not second-order) [formal: acceleratio proprietatum | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

payload.name: perceptual-linear-prediction
payload.scope: People made perceptual linear prediction to produce speech features that model the Bark-scale critical-band structure of human hearing and the nonlinear loudness compression before linear prediction, giving better speaker and background robustness than raw spectral methods.

definition.body: Perceptual linear prediction coefficients are a sequence of features extracted from a speech frame by applying a Bark-scale critical-band filterbank to the power spectrum, compressing the filtered energies with a power-law nonlinearity to model the equal-loudness contours of human hearing, and projecting the compressed energies onto an orthogonal basis via discrete cosine transform. Parameters: (1) the number of Bark filters (typically 13-26); (2) the power-law exponent (typically 1/3); (3) the number of DCT coefficients retained (typically 12-17). Persistence: implemented as the plp feature pipeline in the Kaldi toolkit, as the PLP analysis routine in the HTK toolkit, and as a recognized speech feature alternative to MFCC in the librosa feature extraction interface. e.g.: the plp feature pipeline in Kaldi s3 feature extraction; the PLP coefficients computed by the PLP analysis routine in HTK HCopy for triphone HMM training; the PLP feature vector produced by applying a Bark-scale filterbank with 1/3-power compression and DCT in HTK | not: bark-scale-filterbank (the linear filterbank stage alone, without the power-law compression and DCT projection); cepstral-coefficient (raw DFT-derived coefficients, without the perceptual filterbank and power-law stages) [formal: perceptiva linearis predictio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

definition.body: Perceptual linear prediction coefficients are a sequence of features extracted from a speech frame by applying a Bark-scale critical-band filterbank to the power spectrum, compressing the filtered energies with a power-law nonlinearity to model the equal-loudness contours of human hearing, and projecting the compressed energies onto an orthogonal basis via discrete cosine transform. Parameters: (1) the number of Bark filters (typically 13-26); (2) the power-law exponent (typically 1/3); (3) the number of DCT coefficients retained (typically 12-17). Persistence: implemented as the plp feature pipeline in the Kaldi toolkit, as the PLP analysis routine in the HTK toolkit, and as a recognized speech feature alternative to MFCC in the librosa feature extraction interface. e.g.: the plp feature pipeline in Kaldi s3 feature extraction; the PLP coefficients computed by the PLP analysis routine in HTK HCopy for triphone HMM training; the PLP feature vector produced by applying a Bark-scale filterbank with 1/3-power compression and DCT in HTK | not: bark-scale-filterbank (the linear filterbank stage alone, without the power-law compression and DCT projection); cepstral-coefficient (raw DFT-derived coefficients, without the perceptual filterbank and power-law stages) [formal: perceptiva linearis predictio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

payload.name: log-mel-spectrogram
payload.scope: People made log-mel spectrograms to compress the mel-frequency spectrogram into a perceptually-shaped, energy-density representation that is compact, robust to dynamic range, and well-suited as input for neural network acoustic models.

definition.body: A log-mel spectrogram is the logarithm of the mel-frequency spectrogram, obtained by computing a short-time Fourier transform, mapping the resulting linear frequency bins onto the mel-scale via a triangular filterbank, summing the squared magnitude coefficients within each filter, and applying a base-10 or natural logarithm to compress the dynamic range. Parameters: (1) the window function and hop size (e.g., Hann window, 25ms window, 10ms hop); (2) the number of mel filters (typically 40-128); (3) the mel frequency range (e.g., 0-8000 Hz). Persistence: implemented as the librosa feature mel-spectrogram with log scaling (librosa.feature.melspectrogram + np.log), in the Kaldi featbin compute-fbank feature extraction with log option, and as the torchaudio transforms Melspectrogram + LogOperation in PyTorch audio pipelines. e.g.: librosa feature.melspectrogram with log1p for Kaldi Librispeech ASR; Kaldi compute-fbank with --log-fbank=true for NN acoustic training; torchaudio.transforms.Melspectrogram with log1p in speech recognition training | not: mel-frequency-cepstrum (cepstral coefficients derived from log-mel via DCT, not the log-mel representation itself); mel-filterbank (the linear filterbank before log compression) [formal: logarithmica mel spectographema | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]

payload.name: cepstrum-time-warping
payload.scope: People made cepstral time warping to non-uniformly modify the quefrency axis of a cepstrum, compressing formant-dense regions to improve alignment and speaker robustness.

definition.body: Cepstral time warping is a technique that modifies the quefrency axis of a cepstrum by non-uniform warping to align the temporal structure of speech frames, compressing or expanding low-quefrency regions where formant-related information concentrates while preserving high-quefrency voicing periodicity. The procedure: apply a nonlinear mapping function q' = f(q) to each quefrency value q, where f is typically a logarithmic or power-law function that compresses low quefrencies. The warped cepstrum is then transformed back to the time or frequency domain via inverse transform. Parameters: (1) the warping function (logarithmic, power-law, or custom); (2) the warping parameter controlling compression strength; (3) the quefrency range to warp. Persistence: implemented in cepstral analysis software for speaker normalization and in robust speech recognition front-ends as a preprocessing step before feature extraction. e.g.: cepstral quefrency warping applied for speaker normalization in Kaldi's i-vector extraction pipeline; logarithmic quefrency warping in HTK cepstral analysis for improved formant alignment; custom quefrency warping in the VoiceCept speaker recognition toolkit | not: cepstral-subband (dividing the cepstral domain into frequency bands without non-uniform warping); cepstral-smoothing (low-pass filtering of cepstral coefficients, not quefrency-axis warping) [formal: quefrequenti temporis deformatio | substrate: mind | horizon: a life | explicit: yes]
